facts.raw_span: 7-year history of severe, mechanical, low back pain
long-standing mental depression
self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine, 100 mg 4 times per day, for the past 3 years
Large and deep, irregularly shaped, cutaneous ulcer on the dorsum of right forearm with necrotic tissue and muscle exposure at the base
Woody induration of skin on both forearms and abdominal region
Bilateral contracture of deltoid, triceps, and biceps muscles
Active and passive range of motion restricted at shoulders and elbows
No signs of joint inflammation
Elevated serum creatinine kinase (192 U/L; reference range, 0-174 U/L)
Normal complete blood cell count
Shows lobular panniculitis, subcutaneous fat lobules with necrotic adipocytes and dense inflammatory infiltrates composed mainly of foamy histiocytes
Deltoid muscle biopsy showed no muscle involvement

Foreign-body giant cells and macrophages with large, foamy cytoplasm present
concepts.why: The patient's history of self-administering subcutaneous injections and the presence of foreign-body giant cells suggest a foreign body granuloma.

support_spans: Large and deep, irregularly shaped, cutaneous ulcer on the dorsum of right forearm with necrotic tissue and muscle exposure at the base
contradict_spans: No signs of joint inflammation
Negative culture specimens for bacteria, mycobacteria, and fungal organisms
concepts.why: The presence of a large, deep cutaneous ulcer with necrotic tissue and muscle exposure suggests necrotizing fasciitis, although the lack of joint inflammation and negative culture results argue against it.

support_spans: Large and deep, irregularly shaped, cutaneous ulcer on the dorsum of right forearm with necrotic tissue and muscle exposure at the base
contradict_spans: No evidence of thrombosis or vasculitis
No polarizable foreign material identified

frontier_selector.why: The histopathology showing lobular panniculitis with necrotic adipocytes and dense inflammatory infiltrates composed mainly of foamy histiocytes decided it.
